I'm a 29-year-old woman with no schooling, farming 8 mu in Quzhou. My husband works construction in the city and sends money home. My mother-in-law lives with us and helps with the kids and the field work. There are six of us under the roof, but only me and my mother-in-law are here day-to-day for the farm. I've been working this land since I was little — my parents taught me everything — and I do what they did, what my neighbors do. I don't read books about farming; I watch and remember.

I split my 8 mu the same as always: 5 mu for wheat then maize, and 3 mu for cotton. I thought about planting more cotton because the money is better, but who would pick it? My husband is gone eleven months a year, my father-in-law's back is bad, and hiring pickers costs 2 yuan per kilo. Three mu of cotton is enough for me and my mother-in-law to handle during picking season, especially when the kids help on weekends in autumn.

For wheat, I plant early October, same as everyone in the village. I use seed from my own storage if it looks clean, otherwise I buy from the village shop. Before planting, I spread about half a big bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the shop has it in red bags, I don't know the numbers on it — and till it in with the rotary tiller. Come March, when the wheat is jointing, I walk the field. If it looks yellow, I spread urea, about one bag for every two mu. Water costs electricity for the pump, so I irrigate three times: after planting if it's dry, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once in the spring. For harvest, I hire the combine — 50 yuan per mu — because me and my mother-in-law can't cut five mu by hand before the rains come. I expect about 380 kilos per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got about 370.

Maize goes in 2–3 days after the wheat comes off in June. No time to waste. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, the same kind my neighbor Lao Wang uses, about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow when planting, about half a bag per mu. At big trumpet stage, I look at the leaves. If they're pale, I topdress with urea. I water twice if the sky doesn't give rain. I always spray herbicide and insecticide — the corn borer is bad around here and I can't afford to lose the crop. I usually get 400–450 kilos per mu.

Cotton is planted in late April. It needs the most hand work. I plow in spring, then fertilize three times: base before planting, then urea when the flowers come, and more when the bolls form. I irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. Even though I buy Bt cotton seed, I still spray for bollworm and aphids — I've seen too many people lose their crop trusting the seed alone. Picking is the hardest part. Me, my mother-in-law, and the kids pick by hand through September and October. I expect about 250 kilos per mu of seed cotton.

My husband's wages mean I can buy the fertilizer I need, but I still watch every yuan. Last year I cut back a little on cotton fertilizer to save money and the yield dropped, so this year I won't do that again. I'd rather spend a bit more than risk a bad year. But I also won't put more fertilizer than usual on the wheat just because the shop says I could — what I do already works, and change is risky.
